clue.text: Very happy controlling line in gospel message

parts.note: being on top of something is having it under control

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the line goes within the message

parts.note: the Word is the gospel message preached
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A preacher delighted at being in charge of a line in a gospel reading.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside THE WORD to make THE WORLD, which follows ON TOP OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling on top of the world is an idiom for being elated and exceptionally pleased.

clue.text: Unions reveal bit at work requiring lots of work

indicators.note: letters put to work are being moved about and rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Trade unions disclose something about a demanding job.
explanation.walkthrough: The union surface suggests labour politics, which happens to fit the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour-intensive process needs a great deal of human effort and many workers to carry out.

clue.text: Restaurant quiet about wood floating on river

indicators.note: in a down entry, what floats on something sits directly above it
something placed about another wraps around it on both sides

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
teak is a hardwood
the Ouse is an English river name used by several rivers

explanation.surface: A restaurant built on a timber raft drifting on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the wood-with-quiet sits on top of the river. The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, another in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: A steakhouse is a type of restaurant specialising in grilled beef dishes.

clue.text: When speaking the writer was hard, being 20?

indicators.note: when spoken out, the word for the writer is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter as I, which is heard as the organ of sight
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A writer recalls being stern while talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is a cross-reference to the answer at 20-across, NONSENSE. The writer is the setter, I, and read out that letter is the word for the organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for claptrap or humbug, talk meant to deceive and with no substance.

clue.text: Nasty, uncovering lechery in extreme cases

indicators.note: the extreme cases of words are their ends, so only first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: Revealing lecherous behaviour in the worst cases is unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovering' reads like a verb of exposure but is itself one of the source words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean unpleasant or threatening, as in an ugly mood or ugly scene.

clue.text: Source of floral stuff repurposed in banal decorating

indicators.note: material repurposed is put into a new form, so the letters take new places

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Flower material reused in some dull interior decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical garden grows many plants and flowers, so it supplies floral material in abundance.

clue.text: Deceptive stuff in newspapers supporting donkey being introduced to beach

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting part sits underneath what it holds up
something introduced to a place is brought inside it

parts.note: a beach is made of sand
moke is British and Australian slang for a donkey
the Mirror is a British tabloid, so newspapers can be Mirrors

explanation.surface: Tabloid trickery about a beach donkey being led onto the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper; in a down entry, the supporting newspapers go underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke and mirrors is the stock phrase for misleading tricks that obscure the truth.

clue.text: Still developing latest things in better toy soldiers

parts.note: an infant is still growing and developing

indicators.note: the latest things in words are their final letters

parts.note: the final letters of these two words

explanation.surface: The newest and best toy soldiers are still being designed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toy soldiers' looks like one phrase, but only 'soldiers' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The infantry are foot soldiers collectively, the army arm that fights on foot.

clue.text: Dismal cold house I avoided, one out of many

indicators.note: a letter avoided is left out of the word

parts.note: an igloo is a house of snow and ice
taken as written, the letter removed

indicators.note: taking a piece out of a word removes those letters

parts.note: taken as written
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: A cheerless cold house that someone kept away from, one among many.
explanation.walkthrough: IGLOO loses its I, and AN comes out of MANY to leave MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and dismal are synonyms, both describing dark, depressing and cheerless conditions.

clue.text: Lit one after my cigar

indicators.note: what comes after follows on to the right in an across entry

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
a light that is lit is on
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone lights up after their own cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' looks possessive; it is the exclamation, here the British cor.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a long straight-sided cigar with a rounded end, a standard cigar size.

clue.text: Indicators to assess Groucho on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio words are only heard, so a phrase of the same sound will do

parts.note: to weigh is to assess, and Groucho was the best known of the Marx brothers

explanation.surface: Signs for judging a Groucho Marx comedy broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Waymarks are signs or posts that guide walkers along a route, so they indicate the way.

clue.text: Fell over during unobjectionable music?

indicators.note: something during another happens within it, so it goes inside

parts.note: MOR is middle-of-the-road music, bland and inoffensive
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone toppled during some easy-listening music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb but is the noun: in northern England a fell is a high open hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell and a moor are both stretches of high, open, uncultivated upland in Britain.

clue.text: Chap's court case involving old college at various points in the past

parts.note: his is the possessive belonging to a chap

indicators.note: a case involving something takes it inside
the inserted letters go in at separate places rather than together

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court
O is a standard abbreviation for old
C is a standard abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A man's legal case involves a former college at several stages.
explanation.walkthrough: The old and college letters are not inserted together but at two separate spots in the court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical describes things belonging to or occurring in former times, so it means in the past.

clue.text: NASA's concern: shots off target and rate of progress

parts.note: in archery and shooting an outer is a shot hitting the outer ring rather than the bull
pace is speed of movement

explanation.surface: The space agency worries about missed shots and slow progress.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA is the American space agency, and the region beyond Earth's atmosphere is its business.

clue.text: Decide not to meet comedian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fail to turn up for a date, leaving the other person waiting
second meaning: a comic who performs solo before an audience

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the verb, written open as stand up; the second is the noun, usually hyphenated.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone up is to miss an arranged date, and a stand-up is a solo comic performer.

clue.text: Bears seen around river beaches

indicators.note: something around another encloses it

parts.note: to stand something is to bear or tolerate it
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Bears spotted near a river on its shores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like animals but is the verb to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand is a literary word for a shore or beach, so strands are beaches.

clue.text: Quickly reduced claim with staff being cut

indicators.note: a reduced word has been cut down by its final letter

parts.note: to allege is to claim without proof

indicators.note: a word being cut loses its end

parts.note: a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: A claim shrunk in a hurry as staff are laid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff being cut' suggests job losses; the staff is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a brisk, lively tempo, so it means play fast.

clue.text: Nonconformist mostly tucked into quantity of wine, employing a bit of brain

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it

parts.note: a cellar is a stock of wine

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the word is short of its last letter

parts.note: a rebel refuses to conform

explanation.surface: A rebel half-hidden in a wine supply, putting a little brainpower to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonconformist' with a capital looks like the chapel-going Protestant, but it is just a rebel; 'quantity of wine' is a wine stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebellar means relating to the cerebellum, the part of the brain coordinating movement and balance.

clue.text: Courage shown by former King going to Troy

indicators.note: one part going to another moves along to join it at its side

parts.note: GRI, Georgius Rex Imperator, was the cipher of George V and George VI as King-Emperor
t is the abbreviation for troy weight, as in oz t

explanation.surface: A past king shows bravery by setting off for Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy suggests the Homeric city, but it is the system of weights for precious metals.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is informal for courage and determination, the resolve to keep going in difficulty.

clue.text: Nobody accepting Ness rippling? Rubbish

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in

parts.note: none means not one person

indicators.note: rippling water moves things about, so the letters shift around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: No one admits to seeing ripples on Loch Ness, calling it rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness points to Loch Ness and its monster sightings, a fitting picture for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense and rubbish are both words for foolish talk or ideas without truth or sense.

clue.text: Right to engage in study, turning — into this?

definitions.text: Right to engage in study, turning — into this?

indicators.note: turning round means the whole thing is read the other way
to engage in something is to enter it, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a den is a private study room
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A student hunched over books, turned into a swot by all that study.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone who does nothing but study risks becoming exactly this kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is a bookish, socially awkward person obsessed with study, which over-studying might make you.

clue.text: Right to switch components by agency

indicators.note: switching the components means its two parts change places

parts.note: proper means correct or right

explanation.surface: A right to change component suppliers through an agent.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for right breaks into two three-letter halves that trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: Per pro is Latin per procurationem, used when signing a letter on another person's behalf as their agent.

clue.text: Small piece, not advisable for swell organ

indicators.note: not having something means the word is without it

parts.note: taken as written
well can mean advisable, as in it would be well to wait
the liver is a body organ

explanation.surface: A warning that something is unwise for a church organ's swell box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell organ' reads as part of a pipe organ; SWELL without WELL leaves S, then the body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliver is a thin narrow piece cut or split off something, so a small piece.

clue.text: Aerospace work? Shock European attempt

parts.note: to rock someone is to shock them
E is the abbreviation for European
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A daring European venture into aerospace.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the science and engineering of rockets, one branch of aerospace activity.
